data.exact_reserve_text: An analysis of the claims development - gross

prior_year_events.impact_description: increasing costs reserves for Russia/Ukraine related litigations and adverse loss experience in Aviation

data.standardized_narrative: The syndicate experienced mixed prior year development in 2023, resulting in a net release of GBP 34.385 million, representing 2.58% of opening gross claims outstanding. Favourable developments were noted in the EL/PL book due to re-underwriting efforts. Conversely, adverse developments impacted US Casualty, International Casualty, and Motor books, driven by social and economic inflation, including increases in the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) and anticipated revisions to the UK Personal Injury Discount Rate. The Aviation market also saw adverse experience due to increasing costs reserves related to Russia/Ukraine litigations.
raw_causal_phrases: Actions to strengthen the pricing and reserving of the US Casualty business taken in recent years have been well founded with historic loss experience developing in line with best estimate expectations.

Reserving in these classes has close regard for the anticipated outcomes of legal, social and economic trend and we have further strengthened reserving in some parts of the portfolio to address claims inflation concerns and recent loss experience.

The Aviation market saw a marked slowdown in rates in 2022 and this has not curtailed in 2023. Of particular note Faraday is mindful of on-going issues and litigation that is affecting the market relating to aeroplanes which have been leased to Russian airlines. The book suffered adverse experience in 2023 due to increasing costs reserves for Russia/Ukraine related litigations and adverse loss experience.
The EL/PL book was profitable in 2023 and continues to benefit from the re-underwriting of the book over the past few years. This business also benefited from favourable prior year developments.

The International Casualty and Motor books were adversely impacted by prior year developments and increases in the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) due to heightened inflation in the UK. The syndicate has considered the expected movements in the UK Personal Injury Discount Rate and has reserved for these accordingly including an allowance for the revisions now expected in 2024.

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: The prior year development figure is calculated from the gross claims development triangle. This figure shows a net release, which contrasts with the 'Change in the provision for claims - Gross amount' in the Profit and Loss Account (page 3) which indicates a strengthening. The triangle is considered a more direct measure of prior year development.
